security_frame.attacker: Software that can write the HMAC control register, which is the level at which the zeroize strobe is issued. HMAC512_CTRL is an ordinary MMIO register in the block's own address range, so no physical, debug or supervisor-only access is required.
security_frame.precondition: An HMAC operation has completed, so the block legitimately reports a valid tag. No other state is required.
security_frame.input: A write to HMAC512_CTRL.ZEROIZE while the tag-valid flag is asserted.
security_frame.protected_asset: The truthfulness of the block's completion signalling across a security zeroize: the guarantee that after a zeroize the block reports no valid tag and presents no tag data, so a consumer cannot mistake post-zeroize output for a real result.
security_frame.security_property: A security zeroize is a cleanup operation, so no state that changes the meaning of the block's outputs may survive it. src/hmac/rtl/hmac_core.sv:111-112 make both the 512-bit tag output and the tag_valid output functions of the single register digest_valid_reg, and the file's own reset arm at :185 clears that register, so the file itself treats it as state a full clear must zero.
security_frame.implemented_logic: src/hmac/rtl/hmac_core.sv:181-209 holds three registers in one always_ff named reg_update. The reset arm at :184-187 clears all three, including digest_valid_reg at :185. The zeroize arm at :190-196 clears only two, omitting digest_valid_reg while still forcing the FSM to CTRL_IDLE, and carries a comment at :192-193 claiming the normal update path refreshes that register on a later cycle. The normal update path at :202-203 writes it only when digest_valid_we is raised; the FSM defaults that enable to zero at :329 and the CTRL_IDLE arm at :336-351 raises it only in its next_cmd branch, so an engine sitting idle after a zeroize never performs the refresh the comment promises.

security_feature_bypassed: Truthful completion signalling across a security zeroize. The plan sets out to determine whether the block still reports a valid tag after a zeroize, whether the refresh its own comment promises ever occurs, and whether the stale flag reaches the parent block's tag-capture logic.
proof_goal: Establish on one unmodified hmac_core compiled from the audited checkout that a completed zeroize leaves tag_valid asserted, that the claimed later refresh does not occur across a long idle window, and that the parent's own tag-capture edge expression re-asserts as a result, while a real reset still clears the flag.
proof_style: Directed port-driven simulation of one real DUT with the parent's capture-enable expression reproduced from the parent's own source, paired with a scripted structural audit of the submitted tree and a negative control that adds the omitted assignment.
invariant: For every cycle after a zeroize has been taken and before a new command is issued, hmac_core must report tag_valid = 0.
attacker_model: Unprivileged software at user-level mode, being sufficient to write the block's own HMAC512_CTRL.ZEROIZE field. No physical access and no debug access is needed.
minimum_attack_sequence: Run an HMAC operation to completion so the block reports a valid tag.
Write HMAC512_CTRL.ZEROIZE, which returns the FSM to idle but leaves the tag-validity flag asserted.
Observe that the block continues to claim a valid tag, and that the parent's tag-capture enable re-asserts because the parent's own copy of the flag was cleared by the same zeroize.
controls: control_reset_clears_tag_valid: after reset the block must report no valid tag, showing the harness can observe the cleared state.
control_normal_run_sets_tag_valid: a completed operation must report a valid tag, showing the harness reaches the state under test.
containment_reset_still_clears: a real reset applied after the zeroize must clear the flag, separating this defect from any claim that the flag is unclearable.
The parent capture-edge model opens its tracking window only after the modelled parent register has settled to 1, so the legitimate completion edge cannot be counted as the spurious one.
witness_construction_note: The testbench instantiates one hmac_core and drives it only through its declared ports. There is no force, no deposit and no hierarchical assignment anywhere in the harness. The parent's tag-capture enable is not asserted but recomputed from the parent's own expression at src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:163, with the parent's tag_valid_reg modelled exactly as hmac.sv:196-231 writes it, so the reported consequence follows from the parent's own formula.
expected_evidence: A line showing tag_valid asserted after a completed operation.
A line showing tag_valid still asserted several cycles after a completed zeroize, with the FSM reporting ready.
A line showing tag_valid still asserted after a long idle window, contradicting the comment in the zeroize arm.
A line showing the parent's capture enable re-asserting after the zeroize.
A containment line showing a real reset still clears the flag.

Structural gates over the audited tree covering the arm asymmetry, the FSM path the in-RTL comment relies on, the use the flag is put to, and how the child and parent modules write their own zeroize arms.
success_criteria: checks=6, fails=3 and witness_hits=1 in the directed simulation, with the three failures being the post-zeroize checks.
All structural gates passing with RESULT: PASS.
The negative control flips the identical testbench once the omitted assignment is added: fails=0, the two anti-vacuity covers at 0, and both harness controls plus the containment case still passing.
non_findings: No claim is planned that the stale flag discloses digest material. The child masked cores clear their own digests on the same zeroize, so the tag data presented after a zeroize is expected to be zero; the claim is about false completion signalling, not confidentiality.
No claim is planned that zeroize fails generally. The FSM is returned to idle correctly and the containment case tests that reset still works.
No claim is planned about the masking-entropy chain in the same file, which is a separate matter and is not relied on here.

No claim is planned about the LFSR seed width. The seed path is 384 bits consistently across src/hmac/rtl/hmac.sv:81, src/hmac/rtl/hmac_core.sv:39, the twelve 32-bit seed registers, src/hmac_drbg/rtl/hmac_drbg.sv:55 and src/ecc/rtl/ecc_hmac_drbg_interface.sv:48, matching the 384-bit figure in docs/CaliptraHardwareSpecification.md:1199, so no width inconsistency exists to report.
